title: Multimodal Shallow Alignment: Do Vision-Language Models Have Even Shallower Safety?

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: VLMs are increasingly deployed in consumer apps. If their safety is shallower than text models, multimodal inputs create a qualitatively larger attack surface. High-stakes for deployment decisions.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires running VLMs (LLaVA-1.5-7B), generating adversarial images, applying logit-lens across modalities, and comparing text-only vs. multimodal conditions. VLM setup and multimodal probing is substantially harder than text-only work for beginners.

narrow_scope.reasoning: The multimodal pipeline setup (image+text adversarial inputs, VLM inference, cross-modal probing) plus comparison to text-only baseline is too many moving parts for 30 hours of beginner effort.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Novelty not assessed due to partial Wave 3 completion.
